# Requirement and need fulfillment

Owner direction: specify full, partial and absent fulfillment systematically, including the conditions under which each conclusion applies. Capability coverage and working only some of the time are different concerns.

**Accepted resolution of EOM-03 on 2026-09-27.** The owner accepted the assessment meanings and information contract below in the [conditional fulfillment decision](../../notes/decisions/conditional-fulfillment-semantics.md). This is scoped acceptance within the developing standard; it does not release the whole standard or prescribe a mandatory storage format. The [counterexamples and independent review](../../../source-locators.md#source-7a59588ffc932daa) record the checks and limits.

## Three different claims

1. **Expected contribution:** which requirements an arrangement is intended to address and why its design should help. This is a rationale or prediction, not observed fulfillment.
2. **Requirement fulfillment:** whether the assessed subject satisfies a stated requirement under its applicable conditions, according to the identified evidence and assessment basis.
3. **Need fulfillment:** whether the result helps the person or business in the intended way, considering circumstances, costs and competing needs.

A satisfied specification may leave the need unmet. A useful result does not establish that every requirement was satisfied. NASA's [verification and validation distinction](../../../source-locators.md#source-e041472eec158c9c) supports asking these different questions. The separately [accepted adequacy rule](../ontology/concepts/requirement.md#from-requirement-fulfillment-to-need-fulfillment) connects requirements to needs; EOM-03's assessment meanings do not establish that connection by themselves.

## Criterion result and extent of achievement

Report these separately: **the criterion result**, **what was achieved**, and **the conditions and evidence limits**. Acceptance is a separate decision.

| Criterion result | Meaning at the stated subject, revision and scope |
| --- | --- |
| **Met** | The evidence and stated assessment basis support satisfaction of the criterion. This is not a promise about unexamined situations or future operation. |
| **Unmet** | The evidence and stated assessment basis establish that the criterion is not satisfied. Record the decisive shortfall. |
| **Unknown** | Available evidence or an unresolved criterion/applicability question does not support either conclusion. State what prevents the judgment. |

“Partly met” is not a fourth criterion result under this contract. **Partial fulfillment** remains usable shorthand only when the achieved and unachieved portions or dimensions are identified alongside the criterion result. For example: “Unmet: two of three required explanations passed; one failed.” A threshold requirement can be met despite partial achievement across the entire population.

| Extent description | Meaning and limit |
| --- | --- |
| **Full** | All of the named extent was achieved under the stated conditions. Name that extent: all required functions, all examined cases, or a specified output. These are different claims. |
| **Partial** | Some of the named extent was achieved and some was not. State the parts, counts or qualitative distinctions; do not invent a percentage for an unordered or ordinal judgment. |
| **None** | Adequate evidence establishes zero achievement of the named extent in the stated scope. This is not shorthand for missing evidence. Zero successful transfers need not mean zero bytes transferred. |
| **Extent uncertain** | Evidence leaves achievement unresolved. Report known successes, failures and unknowns or justified bounds. Two successes and two unknowns establish at least two successes; they do not establish that the actual extent was exactly partial. |

Use raw quantities and explanations when these extent labels add nothing. Failure to meet a deadline does not mean no useful output exists. Neither an arbitrary score nor an average across different dimensions replaces the criterion judgment.

## Assessment contract

The following is the minimum information needed to interpret an assessment, not eight mandatory duplicated YAML fields. It may be stated briefly or linked from an exact applicable record. Missing information stays explicit.

| Information | What the reader must be able to recover |
| --- | --- |
| Subject | The system, combined arrangement, capability claim or occurrence; relevant version/configuration and boundary. |
| Requirement and criterion | The statement/revision; what counts as success; relevant quantifier, threshold, units, denominator, deadline/window or qualitative judgment basis. Do not invent missing requirements. |
| Applicability | Required users, inputs, cases and operating conditions; explicit exclusions and their basis. |
| Examined scope | Which conditions, cases and times were actually examined; whether this is a complete finite set, sample, analysis or other justified basis. |
| Achievement and evidence | Observations or justified inferences, supporting records, counts/measurements where useful, and any missing, disputed or unreliable evidence. Stipulated examples must be labeled as such. |
| Conclusion | Met/unmet/unknown for the stated scope, with the reason and the extent actually supported. |
| Assessment provenance | Who assessed, when, which evidence was available and what reasoning or referenced method supports the conclusion. |
| Acceptance, when relevant | The separate decision, authority and conditions, or that no acceptance decision is recorded. Omit the decision field when acceptance is not part of the use case. |

No automatic confidence percentage is required. Explain uncertainty. If a confidence level or qualitative confidence scale is used, identify its meaning, basis and applicable scope. Subjective confidence is not a measured fulfillment rate.

## Conditions and uncertainty

**Required conditions must not shrink to match examined conditions.** If offline operation is required but unexamined, retain it as required and report that finding as unknown, with “required offline condition unexamined” as the reason. A genuinely excluded route can be not applicable under the requirement's scope rule; it is not a successful case. If applicability itself is uncertain, preserve that question rather than exclude the case.

“Not assessed” describes the absence of an assessment, not a fulfillment outcome. Do not infer failure or success from it. Before a deadline or observation window closes, describe current progress or a provisional result unless the criterion is already decisively established.

Assessing the available information and concluding “unknown” is itself an assessment. In the offline example, the missing activity is examination of the required offline condition, not the assessment that reports that evidence gap. Keep those activities distinct without introducing another fulfillment result.

Missing or credible conflicting evidence affects the conclusions it could change. Do not silently choose a favorable record. Resolve conflict under an identified basis or retain the affected result as unknown. A separately established failure can still defeat an all-cases criterion even when other cases are unknown. Conversely, a threshold can already be satisfied despite unresolved cases.

Evidence can include justified analysis or qualitative judgment; every real-world occurrence need not be directly observed. Any conclusion beyond examined cases must identify the inference and its assumptions. A sample of ten successes is bounded evidence of performance; it does not by itself guarantee future reliability. The [NIST source account](../../../source-locators.md#source-b4223c00cce2432d) distinguishes an observed proportion from inference about a population parameter. Statistical and verification methods remain separately scoped.

## A precise rule for finite counts

For a **known, fixed set of N equally counted cases**, let S be established successes, F established failures and U unresolved cases; S + F + U = N. Classification uses the same criterion, subject revision and time window for every case. No case is counted twice.

For a criterion **at least K successes**:

- Met when S >= K.
- Unmet when S + U < K.
- Unknown otherwise.

Thus for S = 8, F = 1 and U = 1: all ten is unmet; at least eight is met; at least nine is unknown. Achievement remains eight known successes, one known failure and one unknown in each assessment. The facts did not change; the criterion did.

This bounded counting rule does not require independence between cases. It is not a reliability estimator or a default scoring formula for weighted or qualitative judgments. With unknown membership or an open-ended denominator, do not invent N or use these equations without justified bounds. A zero-case window does not establish successful execution or capability; a counting predicate and the operational meaning of an empty window are separate. State any empty-window rule explicitly.

For an all-cases criterion, one established failure is decisive. For an at-least-one criterion, one established success is decisive. Multiple requirements can only be summarized under their declared combination rule: all mandatory criteria, specified alternatives or a separately justified rubric. Do not average their scores or infer whole-system fulfillment from component success.

## Dimensions to preserve

| Dimension | Report what it measures |
| --- | --- |
| Capability coverage | Which functions or cases the arrangement is supported as able to handle, under which conditions and on what evidence. One successful occurrence and an enduring capability are different claims. |
| Frequency or reliability | Successes/failures/unknowns over a defined set or time interval; distinguish observed frequency from estimated future reliability and state the basis of any estimate. |
| Performance or quality | Actual values or qualitative findings against the relevant criteria, with units or a judgment rubric. “280 ms against a 250 ms limit” is clearer than an invented fulfillment percentage. |
| Conditional applicability | Results for materially different operating conditions, with required and examined scope both visible. |
| Evidence sufficiency | What is established, uncertain, disputed or missing; uncertainty does not measure how much of a need is fulfilled. |
| Acceptance | Who decided to accept, reject or conditionally use the result. An authorized waiver or acceptance does not make a known unmet criterion met. |

Use only the dimensions relevant to the claim. A baseline is needed when the criterion concerns improvement from a baseline; it is not a universal field for every assessment.

## Illustrative cases, not run evidence

| Existing case | Criterion result | Achievement and limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Personal P1](../../examples/personal-learning-review.md), Week A | Unmet for the all-three weekly criterion. | Two explanations pass, one fails. Offline operation remains unexamined. Neither this count nor P2's independent success establishes later useful understanding. |
| Personal P2, Week A | Met for the stipulated week. | A complete 95-minute time record is within 120 minutes. It does not establish P1 or future weeks. |
| [Business B1](../../examples/business-payroll-handoff.md), Cycle A | Unmet for the all-four deadline criterion. | Two correct on-time credits, one known missed deadline and one unknown result. Missing evidence for D does not erase C's failure or turn D into a known failure. |
| Business B2, Cycle A | Met for the submission criterion. | The submitted file/register comparison and bank receipt support the judgment. Bank file acceptance does not establish credit or discharge the payment obligation. |

The earlier five-topic example follows the same rule: five of five checked topics with usable references meet that finite-set criterion; three of five do not, while retaining 60% observed passing coverage. Unexamined topics and future periods remain outside that finding. “More room for curiosity” can use an explicit human judgment and supporting observations; it need not acquire an invented numerical scale.

## Compact report

For the fictional payroll case, the same result can be read without reconstructing the whole model:

> **Subject:** joint payroll arrangement, Configuration A, Cycle A.  
> **Requirement:** B1 revision A; all four correct credits by Friday 17:00 UTC.  
> **Result:** unmet; C missed the deadline.  
> **Achievement:** A and B credited correctly on time; C not on time; D unknown.  
> **Conditions and evidence:** the four domestic-account payments; the case's stipulated payment records and C's stipulated non-credit establish the result; D has no payment-level record. Other cycles and unexamined failure conditions remain outside this finding.  
> **Assessed by/at:** the fictional payroll lead, Cycle A Friday 17:15 UTC.  
> **Acceptance:** file acceptance concerned B2; broader payment resolution remains open.

The linked case owns the exact requirement, source records and scenario assumptions. This display is an example, not a new frontmatter schema or a requirement to duplicate every referenced fact.

## Time, changed evidence and need fulfillment

Monday recovery can resolve an unpaid balance without satisfying Friday's deadline. New evidence proving an on-time Friday payment can instead change a previously unknown historical assessment. Preserve the previous assessment, new evidence, changed conclusion and reason. A changed requirement creates a different assessment basis; do not silently overwrite the old one. Relevant changes of subject configuration, conditions or evidence can require reassessment.

Need fulfillment receives its own scoped judgment, reasons and evidence. Meeting requirements supports it only through the stated adequacy argument. Costs and competing needs may change usefulness even when the selected requirements are met. Where no criterion has been chosen, record the observed benefit or stakeholder judgment without inventing a pass/fail threshold.

EOM-03's accepted resolution is the separation of criterion result, extent, conditions/evidence and acceptance, with the finite-count rule as one precise application. The [owner decision](../../notes/decisions/conditional-fulfillment-semantics.md) resolves F3; EOM-03 is closed in the [shared ledger](../../../source-locators.md#source-b7fdccb96a6dde23). The separate [adequacy decision](../../notes/decisions/requirements-to-needs-adequacy.md) resolves F2/EOM-02. EOM-04 and EOM-07 retain their distinct conceptual scope. Detailed implementation and verification methods remain outside this page.
